chunks: 5520 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from 'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the orphan girl: when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: "When you know that she neither corrupts nor wastes it."
So I asked him: if she has married? He said: "When she marries, the authority of the guardian over her has ended."
The author of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: By that he means when she reaches nine years of age.

key_terms.الْيَتِيمَةِ: the orphan girl whose legal and financial status is being discussed
key_terms.تُضَيِّعُ: to waste or neglect the property
key_terms.تُفْسِدُ: to misuse or corrupt the property
key_terms.تِسْعَ سِنِينَ: nine years of age, as explained by the compiler
key_terms.مَالُهَا: her property or wealth held on her behalf
key_terms.مُلْكُ الْوَصِيِّ: the guardian's authority or control over her affairs

ai.seo_question: When should an orphan girl's wealth be given to her in Shia fiqh, and what changes after her marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about when an orphan girl's property may be handed over to her: when she is known to be responsible and not wasteful. It also states that upon marriage, the guardian's authority over her ends, and the compiler explains this as referring to her reaching nine years of age.
